THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:

JUDGMENT Heard Sri K.R. Nagaraj, learned counsel for the appellant and Sri Srinivas Bhat, learned counsel for respondent No.1.
2.
Unsuccessful plaintiff has preferred the present appeal challenging the validity of the judgment and decree passed in O.S.No.2154/1994 dated 27.08.2007 in this appeal.
3. Parties are referred to as plaintiff and defendants for the sake of convenience as per their original ranking in the Trial Court.

4. Brief facts of the case are as under:
NC: 2023:KHC:28825 Plaintiff has filed a suit in O.S.No.2154/1994 with a prayer of passing of permanent injunction to restrain the defendants from interfering with the peaceful possession and enjoyment of the property constructed on site bearing No.26 formed out of Sy.No.40/1 of Nagavara village, Kasaba Hobli, Bengaluru North Taluk,
measuring East-West 30 feet, North to South 40 feet, together with building thereon and bounded on the East by site No.1, west by site No.27, North by private property Smt L A Radha vs Bangalore Development Authority on 14 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145206128/
2 and South by 20 feet road (hereinafter referred to as 'suit property').
5.

sentences.text: The case of the plaintiff is that one Guttappa was the owner of land in Sy.No.40/1 of Nagavara village, Kasaba Hobli, Bengaluru North Taluk, Bengaluru District.
He was in actual physical possession of the said property and since the land became unfit for cultivation, he decided to form the house sites in the said land.
He also offered that the revenue house sites formed by him for the public for sale.
Plaintiff accordingly, purchased site No.26 formed in the land bearing Sy.No.40/1 of Nagavara village, which is the suit property.

Since there was a restriction for sale and registration of the revenue sites, plaintiff entered into an agreement of sale with Guttappa in respect of NC:
2023:KHC:28825 the suit property and a power of attorney.

An affidavit came to be executed in favour of plaintiff and put the plaintiff in possession of the property and from that day onwards,
plaintiff is in possession of the suit property and enjoyed the same by constructing the building thereon.

6. It is further contended that the land was not to be acquired by Bengaluru Development Authority and plaintiff was not dispossessed from the land and therefore, plaintiff continued to be in the suit property.
When Bengaluru Development Authority tried to demolish the structure in the suit property, plaintiff approached the Civil Court for the relief of permanent injunction.

7. In pursuance of suit summons issued, first defendant - Bengaluru Development Authority appeared before the Court and filed detailed written statement contending that the plaintiff did not derive any right, title and interest over the suit property by virtue of the agreement to sell, power of attorney and the affidavit said to have been executed by Guttappa in her favour and sought for dismissal of the suit property.

First defendant also brought to the notice of the Court in the form of written statement that an earlier suit came to be filed in O.S.No.1607/1988 almost for the similar relief which came to be dismissed on 30.09.1993 and therefore, sought for dismissal of the suit.

9. Bengaluru Development Authority also took up the contention that statutory notice as contemplated under Section 64 of Bengaluru Development Authority Act has not been complied and therefore, suit is to be dismissed.
10. Defendant Nos.2 and 3 remained exparte.

11. Based on the rival contentions of the parties, the Trial Court framed the following issues:
1. Whether the plaintiff proves her lawful possession over the suit property and construction of house- building on the suit property?
2.
Whether the plaintiff proves that an illegal attempt was made, by the officials of the 1st defendant to demolish the building?

3 3.

sentences.text: Whether the suit is bad for non-compliance of Section 64 of the BDA Act?
Whether the defendant proves that the suit property had been duly acquired by it and that the suit cannot maintain?
5. To what decree/order, the parties are entitled?
12. In order to prove the case of the plaintiff, plaintiff got examined herself as P.W.1 and one witness Smt. Varalakshmi as P.W.2.

Plaintiff relied on 29 documentary evidence on record which were exhibited and marked as Exs.P.1 to 29 comprising of certified copy of the order passed in case No.ULC(A) 282/1985-86 dated 25.04.1980 as Ex.P.1, General power of attorney dated 23.11.1985 as Ex.P.2, affidavit, jointly sworn to by Shriyuths Guttappa and Parthasarathy as Ex.P.3, certified copy of the sale deed dated 11.10.1982 as Ex.P.4, sale agreement dated 11.10.1982 as Ex.P.5, rental agreement as Ex.P.6, tax paid receipt as Ex.P.7, tax paid receipt as Ex.P.8, katha registration as Ex.P.9, katha certificate as Ex.P.10, katha extract as Ex.P.11, electricity bills as Exs.P.12 to P.16,
encumbrance certificate as Ex.P.17, photographs with negatives as Exs.P.18 and P.19, demand bills issued by BWSSB as Exs.P.20 and P.22, telephone bills as Exs.P.23 to P.25, ration card as Ex.P.26,
electoral identity card as Ex.P.27, copy NC: 2023:KHC:28825 of the legal notice as Ex.P.28, postal acknowledgement as Ex.P.29.
13.

To counter the evidence placed by the plaintiff on behalf of the defendant No.1 - Bengaluru Development Authority, Sri B.S. Ravishankar has been examined as D.W.1 and he has produced copy of the preliminary notification dated 29.5.1978 and copy of final notification dated 28.02.1985 which were marked as Exs.D.1 and D.2.
14.

On conclusion of the recording of evidence, the Trial Court heard the parties in detail and dismissed the suit of the plaintiff holding that the plaintiff failed to establish that plaintiff is in lawful possession and enjoyment of the suit property.
15. Being aggrieved by the said judgment and decree, the plaintiff has preferred the present appeal on the following grounds:

The Learned Judge of the Trial Court has erred in failing to see that the land bearing Sy.No 40/1, measuring 1 acre 28 guntas was originally belonging to the deceased Guttappa who has been arrayed as plaintiff in the above suit and he has NC:
2023:KHC:28825 formed revenue sites over the said land and sold in favour of different persons and among them the suit site bearing Sy.No.26, measuring East to West 30 ft and North to South 40 ft. is sold by Guttappa in favour of the appellant by way of Agreement of Sale dt 11.10.1982 for a valuable consideration and put the appellant in physical possession of the same by receiving the sale consideration amount.

4

sentences.text: Thereafterwards, he has also executed a GPA in favour of the appellant on 23.11.1985, which are marked as Ex. P2 to P5.

The Learned Judge has come to the conclusion that Appellant Radha filed her evidence affidavit contending her evidence as if she herself is the plaintiff in possession and enjoyment of the suit property and inadvertently the name of Guttappa has been shown as plaintiff and represented as GPA holder to him in the cause title, but actually the appellant herself is the plaintiff and in possession and enjoyment of the same having acquired the same by way of Agreement of Sale and GPA executed by Guttappa, but the Trial Court was pleased to see that even the pleadings of the entire plaintiff are also that of as if the appellant has filed the suit against the respondent for the relief of permanent injunction, but not as if the suit is filed by Guttappa, the appellant has represented herself NC: 2023:KHC:28825 as GPA holder of Guttappa, but some mistake crept in while mentioning the name in the cause title as Guttappa represented by GPA holder, the appellant herein has been taken into consideration by the Trial Court though the same is curable defect and negligible point the Trial Court has made it one of the grounds for dismissal of the suit, which is not sustainable in law.

The Learned Judge of the Trial Court has come to the conclusion that Guttappa who is shown as plaintiff in the cause title and the plaintiff is his GPA holder and that Guttappa died during pendency of the suit.

The Learned Judge of the Trial Court except the fact of curable mistake crept in while mentioning the cause title that Guttappa is the plaintiff represented by the appellant herein is not at all looked into the documents showing that she is in possession and enjoyment of the suit property based on the agreement of sale and GPA executed by deceased Guttappa, which are coupled together.

The Learned Judge of the Trial Court has erred in failing to see that Ex P2 executed by Guttappa in favour of the appellant along with Ex.P5 Agreement of Sale and delivered possession of the schedule property in favour of the appellant on the basis of - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:28825 which the appellant has come in possession and enjoyment of the same and she is entitled for the relief of permanent injunction.

The Learned Judge of the Trial Court has erred in failing to see that the appellant has put up construction over the suit property and the same is existing as on the date of filing of the suit as could be seen from the Ex. P.19- photographs.

The Leaned Judge of the Trial Court has erred in failing to see that the revenue records such as khatha etc. pertaining to the suit property have been transferred in the name of the appellant and the appellant has been paying the taxes to the concerned authorities regularly and produced documentary evidence at Ex P7 to P11, which are conclusive proof in possession of the appellant in respect of the suit property.

sentences.text: The Learned Judge of the Trial Court has erred in failing to see that the appellant has let out the schedule property in favour of the tenant Varalakshmi under Ex. P6 in support of the same, the appellant has examined PW-2 who is a tenant under her and the Learned Judge has failed to consider the same in a proper and perspective manner.

The Learned Judge of the Trial Court has also erred in failing to see that the residential house existing over the suit property had water, electricity and telephone connections and the appellant has been paying the respective bills from time to time, which are produced at Ex P.16 The documents produced by the appellant such as Ex P.16, 23, 24, 25 and 27 also prove possession of the appellant over the suit property.

The learned Judge of the Trial Court has not at all taken into consideration the Ex. P1 to P29 produced by the appellant in support of her case to prove that she is in physical possession and enjoyment of the suit property and has passed the judgment and decree is wrong notion that the suit is filed by Guttappa and not appellant herein.

The Leaned Judge of the Trial Court has erred in failing to see that the appellant has proved Issue No.1 beyond reasonable doubt by producing sufficient documents and by adducing oral evidence,
but the Trial Court has wrongly answered Issue No.1 in negative instead of answering the same in affirmative.

The learned Judge of the Trial Court has erred in failing to see that the appellant has also proved that the respondent No 1 officials are making - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC:28825 attempts to interfere with the plaintiff's possession and trying to demolish the structure put up by the appellant over the suit property and the evidence given by DW-1 on behalf of the respondent No 1 claiming that the property in question is acquired by them clearly shows their intention to interfere with the possession of the appellant and thus, the Trial Court ought to have answered Issue No.2 also in favour of the appellant instead of answering the same in negative.

The Trial Court ought to have decreed the suit of the appellant by answering the Issue No. 5 in affirmative on the other hand the Judge of the Trial Court has answered the Issue No.5 also in negative and dismissed the suit of the appellant.

16. Sri. K.R. Nagaraj, learned counsel representing the plaintiff reiterated the grounds urged in the appeal memorandum and contended that the Trial Court has grossly erred in appreciating the possession of the plaintiff, supported by the sale agreement, power of attorney and the affidavit which is the established method of conveying the revenue sites and therefore, Trial Court ought to have decreed the suit of the plaintiff and sought for allowing the appeal.

6 - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC:28825 17.

sentences.text:
He also contended that mere producing Exs.D.1 and D.2, Bengaluru Development Authority did not establish before the Trial Court that plaintiff dispossessed from the suit property inasmuch as there is no award copy that has been filed in respect of the suit property and in the absence of the same and compensation being paid and re-conveyance application not being properly considered,
the plaintiff ought not to have been denied the relief of permanent injunction restraining the defendant - Bengaluru Development Authority from interfering with the peaceful possession and enjoyment of the suit property and sought for allowing the appeal.

18. Per contra, Sri Srinivas Bhat, learned counsel representing Bengaluru Development Authority vehemently contended that the land in question was notified by Bengaluru Development Authority as per the land provisions of Acquisition Act by issuing the preliminary notification dated 29.05.1978 marked at Ex.D.1 and copy of the final notification dated 28.02.1985 marked at Ex.D.2 and therefore, the contentions urged on behalf of the plaintiff that plaintiff was put into possession of the property is incorrect inasmuch as the - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC:28825 agreement Ex.P.5 came to be executed on 11.10.1982 after the preliminary notification and before the final notification came to be passed and whatever the rights, if any, that is said to have been conveyed to the plaintiff by the land owner Sri Guttappa would have merged into the final notification and therefore, the only right that would be available for the plaintiff is to seek for the portion of the compensation from erstwhile owner - Sri Guttappa.
He also contended that possession of the plaintiff, if any, is thus illegal and sought for dismissal of the appeal.
19. In view of the rival contentions of the parties, this Court perused the material on record meticulously.

On such perusal of the material on record, following points would arise for consideration:
1.
Whether the plaintiff has made out a case that he is in lawful possession and enjoyment of the suit property and thus entitled for decree of the suit?
2. Whether the impugned judgment is suffering from legal infirmity and perversity and thus calls for interference?
3. What order?

- 15 - NC: 2023:KHC:28825 Smt L A Radha vs Bangalore Development Authority on 14 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145206128/
7 20.

entities.text: L A Radha vs Bangalore Development Authority
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the case on hand, there is no dispute that the land in Sy.No.40/1 was belonging to Sri Guttappa.
He has executed an agreement to sell on 11.10.1982 in favour of the plaintiff vide Ex.P.5.
The material on record also discloses that Guttappa has executed a power of attorney and an affidavit whereby it is said to have put the plaintiff in possession of the revenue site bearing No.26.
However, as per Ex.D.1, land was notified for the purpose of acquisition by issuing preliminary notification dated 29.05.1978.
Preliminary notification was also published in the newspaper.
It is for the plaintiff to verify into the notification dated 29.05.1978 and should have transacted with the erstwhile owner.
In pursuance of the preliminary notification, final notification came to be issued on 28.02.1985 and possession of the entire land in Sy.No.40/1 vested with the Bengaluru Development Authority.
Thus, the only remedy for the landowner was to receive the compensation from Bengaluru Development Authority.

21. It is now settled principles of law and requires no emphasis that as soon as the final notification and award came to be passed by the Bengaluru Development Authority, all the rights in respect of acquired land would automatically vest with - 16 - NC: 2023:KHC:28825 Bengaluru Development Authority and if any rights that were existing in the erstwhile owner would automatically merged in the final notification issued by Bengaluru Development Authority.

22. Further, mere non marking of the award by Bengaluru Development Authority itself would not make out a case for the plaintiff to claim that she continued to be in lawful possession of the suit property.
23. Taking note of these aspects of the matter, the learned Trial Judge has rightly dismissed the suit of the plaintiff holding that plaintiff is in lawful possession of the property.

24. On re-appreciation of the entire material evidence on record, especially notifying the land for acquisition by preliminary notification and final notification marked at Exs.D.1 and D.2 which are not disputed by the plaintiff, the alleged possession of the suit property by the plaintiff cannot be termed as lawful possession which is sine qua non for maintaining a suit for permanent injunction.

Taking note of these aspects of the matter in view of the foregoing discussion, this Court is of the considered opinion that the plaintiff has failed to establish lawful possession over the suit property.
As such dismissal of the suit by the Trial Court is thus based on proper appreciation of material facts based on sound principles of law.
Hence, the impugned judgment does not call for interference.
Accordingly, point Nos.1 and 2 are answered in the Negative.
